source.title: CLOUD: A Scalable and Physics-Informed Foundation Model for Crystal Representation Learning
source.authors: Chang-Wen Xu; Shang Zhu; Venkat Viswanathan

record.tranche_reason: Extends neural scaling-law analysis to a crystal-materials foundation model and reports its own pretraining-loss and compute-allocation fits.
record.gate_note: The scaling analysis measures CLOUD's pretraining cross-entropy loss while varying pretraining tokens and non-embedding parameters. Downstream benchmark scores and cited scaling-law results are not rows because they do not measure the scaling behavior at issue.
record.test_reason: The study fits a Hoffmann-form power law to the pretraining cross-entropy of CLOUD, a BERT-style masked language model on SCOPE crystal strings. It varies non-embedding parameters and tokens and derives the compute-optimal split. This is a new setting (crystal-structure sequences) with its own result on the scaling form and the allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that NLP scaling laws also apply to crystal foundation models, and that CLOUD scales strongly with model and data size, closely matching Hoffmann's framework (balanced N and D). They note diminishing returns as loss nears the low fitted floor E=0.2296, far below Hoffmann's 1.69. They suggest further gains need better representations or more crystal data.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a transformer and a Hoffmann-style fit to pretraining cross-entropy, but on SCOPE crystal strings with masked-language-model pretraining rather than the original natural-language model setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The loss fit uses the stated Hoffmann form, Huber loss on log loss with δ = 10⁻³, and L-BFGS with multiple random initializations. No comparison of alternative fitting choices or schedules is reported.
record.problems: The text does not state the parameter/token ranges or give individual scaling-sweep losses, uncertainty estimates for the fitted coefficients, or an independent test of large-run extrapolations. The asymptotic behavior is described from the fitted curve.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant scaling results reported beyond r1–r3. Downstream benchmark results and cited scaling results were excluded because they do not measure the claim’s scaling quantities.

untested.parts: Natural-language held-out loss is not studied; the crystal-string result is filed under V5.
There is no check of small-run fits against much larger runs. The 12-layer benchmark model is not reported as a held-out extrapolation point.
No direct IsoFLOP or frontier measurement of optimal N and D. No comparison across schedules or data setups.
Depth and heads were varied only to change size; there is no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Only crystal-string MLM pretraining. No image/video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer scaling.
Downstream scores are not related to scale or to pretraining loss. The with/without pretraining comparison is not a scaling curve.
No comparison of fitting method, parameter counting or schedule. Fitted α=0.43 and β=0.35 are mentioned alongside cited Hoffmann values, but the study does not test the dependence.

missing.what: Scaling-sweep configurations (BERT layers {1,3,6,12}, heads {1,4,12}, embedding 768) and the empirical loss points shown in Fig. 3a/b. These are needed to judge scale range (orders of magnitude) and fit quality.

record.verdict_notes: V7 label removed. Approaching E is a property of the Hoffmann functional form, not evidence of fit-dependence or a bend away from a power law. Most of the paper (MatBench, Discovery, UnconvBench, CLOUD-DEBYE) does not bear on any version. Fig. 3b compares compute-optimal predicted loss with empirical points, but these are in-sample, not a V2 extrapolation test.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a crystal-materials masked-language-model objective, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
No independent evaluation is reported of predictions from small runs against runs orders of magnitude larger.
Does not compare multiple training schedules, model/data setups, or parameter-count conventions.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests crystal-material pretraining only; does not test image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling.
Does not measure whether downstream task performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
Reports one scaling fit and a high-compute asymptote, but does not test how exponents or allocation change with fitting choices or setup.

rows.subject: CLOUD
rows.size_stated: Benchmark model: 12 hidden layers and 12 attention heads; scaling experiments used smaller models, exact sizes not stated.
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of pretraining tokens and non-embedding encoder parameters; fitted the Hoffmann scaling law to pretraining cross-entropy loss.

conditions.value: Tokens D and non-embedding parameters N
Hoffmann scaling law; Huber loss on log loss with δ = 10⁻³; L-BFGS with multiple random initializations

rows.measure: Pretraining cross-entropy loss as a function of tokens and non-embedding parameters
rows.locator: Results, “Transferable and scalable crystal representation learning with CLOUD”; Fig. 3a; Methods, “Scaling Analysis”
rows.note: The authors report that empirical pretraining loss follows the fitted scaling relationship. The text does not state the scale range or give the individual empirical loss values.
rows.check: Link to V5 is right: the setting is crystal-structure strings, not natural-language text. Under V5 the record's V1 'not tested' is defensible. The loss split is not stated: pretraining used an 80/20 train/validation split, but the scaling loss is not called held-out. Sweep sizes are only bounded by Table S1 (BERT layers {1,3,6,12}, heads {1,4,12}). Token counts and per-run losses are not given. No goodness-of-fit is reported.

rows.subject: CLOUD
rows.size_stated: Scaling experiments used smaller models; exact sizes not stated.
rows.operation_detail: Derived the compute-optimal parameter and data allocation from the fitted scaling exponents.

conditions.value: Fixed compute; total compute expressed in FLOPs
Compute-optimal allocation derived from fitted α = 0.4339 and β = 0.3518

rows.value: For CLOUD, a = 0.45 and b = 0.55; the text says parameter and token counts should be scaled evenly.
rows.locator: Results, “Transferable and scalable crystal representation learning with CLOUD”; Eqs. (5)–(6); Fig. 3
rows.note: The paper contrasts these fitted exponents with cited Kaplan values a = 0.73, b = 0.27 and Hoffmann values a = 0.46, b = 0.54; those cited results are not study rows.
rows.check: a=0.45 and b=0.55 come analytically from the fitted α and β (Eq. 6). They are not from an IsoFLOP or frontier measurement, so 'grows as a power' holds by construction of the form. The substantive result is that a≈b, matching Hoffmann rather than Kaplan.

rows.subject: CLOUD
rows.size_stated: Scaling experiments used smaller models; exact sizes not stated.
rows.operation_detail: Examined the high-compute behavior of the fitted cross-entropy-loss curve.

conditions.value: Increasing compute budget; exact threshold not stated
Hoffmann scaling law with entropy term E = 0.2296

rows.measure: Pretraining cross-entropy loss at high compute
rows.value: The fitted loss asymptotically approaches E = 0.2296; the authors state that scaling benefits diminish as compute increases.
rows.note: This is the authors’ description of the fitted curve; no separate numerical high-compute observations or threshold are stated.
rows.check: Loss approaching E is built into the fitted Hoffmann form (irreducible term), not evidence that curves bend away from a power law. It also says nothing about fit-choice or setup dependence, so it does not measure V7. No alternative fits, schedules or parameter conventions are compared.

relationships.condition: CLOUD masked-LM pretraining on ~6.3M crystal strings, models up to 12 layers
relationships.reason: Pretraining loss is fitted by L=A/N^α+B/D^β+E (α=0.434, β=0.352) and the authors say the empirical loss follows it (r1). Scale range and fit quality are not stated.
relationships.display_finding: Pretraining loss followed an additive power law with parameter exponent 0.434 and data exponent 0.352.

relationships.condition: Compute-optimal split derived from the CLOUD parametric fit
relationships.reason: Derived a=0.45 and b=0.55 are close to Hoffmann's 0.46/0.54, so N and D scale about equally (r2). The values are analytic from the fit, not measured on a frontier.
relationships.display_finding: Analytically derived parameter and data exponents were 0.45 and 0.55, near Hoffmann's 0.46/0.54.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
